scoring_justification: Full recompute of hardness from raw DFT outputs infeasible in verifier sandbox; result-level comparison with tolerance, derived moduli recompute consistency, and structural trend checks.

hidden_assets.purpose: Reference averaged lattice parameters, elastic constants, moduli, hardness, and ordering for all nine compounds.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Extracted from Table 1 (averaged rows) and Table 2 (averaged rows) of the paper.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Values transcribed directly from the paper's published tables and cross-verified with the solve.sh that writes the same numbers.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the paper's headlined results; they represent the true computed quantities that a correct reproduction must match within tolerance.

outputs.description: Averaged structural, elastic, and hardness properties for each 5d TM monocarbide. Mechanically unstable compounds have empty derived columns. The verifier compares against hidden paper reference values using tolerances appropriate for a different DFT code.

output_contract.notes: The CSV must contain one row per compound (9 compounds). Compounds with negative C44 must have empty cells in columns B, G, E, nu, fm, Hv, while still reporting their elastic constants and lattice parameters.

steps.description: Verify file exists, required columns present, exactly 9 rows, and all expected compound names are present and only those.
Compare a0 and c0 to paper reference values with relative tolerance 3%.
Compare the five independent elastic constants to paper reference. Use relative tolerance 15% for positive constants, absolute tolerance 10 GPa for negative C44.
Recompute Voigt-Reuss-Hill B, G, E, nu from reported elastic constants for stable compounds and verify consistency with reported values (absolute tolerance 1e-4).
Verify that LaC, HfC, AuC are reported with negative C44 and that B, G, E, nu, fm, Hv are empty.
Compare Hv for mechanically stable compounds to paper reference with relative tolerance 15%.
Verify that hardness of stable compounds follows decreasing order: WC > ReC > TaC > OsC > IrC > PtC.
